claims.text: Stable coherent nanoprecipitates can be present in tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces diminish local stress concentrations associated with premature crack initiation.
Coherent nanoprecipitates increase high-temperature plastic-strain capability in tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
Coherent nanoprecipitates increase high-temperature toughness under fusion-relevant conditions.
The baseline is a spark-plasma-sintered tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy without nanoprecipitate engineering.
Stepwise coherent nanoprecipitates can be introduced and controlled through alloy processing.
In situ monitoring can ensure that nanoprecipitate coherence is maintained during processing and testing.
The proposed comparison uses tensile and creep tests at 800–1000 °C in a fusion-plasma-relevant atmosphere.
The relevant structural mediator is a population of coherent nanoprecipitates embedded in the alloy matrix.
The nanoprecipitate distribution and interface quality remain intact during high-temperature operation.
Nanoprecipitate coherence moderates an interplay between continuous dislocation glide and barrier slip.
At 800–1000 °C, the SCCP-containing alloy will have higher ductility than the unperturbed baseline.
At 800–1000 °C, the SCCP-containing alloy will have greater toughness than the unperturbed baseline.
The SCCP-containing alloy will show reduced strain localization relative to the baseline.
The SCCP-containing alloy will show a measurable change in creep rate relative to the baseline.
The SCCP-containing alloy will show a measurable change in strain-hardening behavior relative to the baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies to coherent-precipitate tungsten-based alloys at 800–1000 °C.
Extreme thermal aging can coarsen the precipitates and compromise the proposed mechanism.
A lack of statistically significant improvement in ductility, toughness, and controlled strain behavior relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes extreme aging and assumes maintained precipitate coherence, whereas the falsification rule treats coarsening and loss of coherence as falsification. Coarsening would remove the stipulated mediator and move the experiment outside the stated validity boundary rather than directly refute the mechanism.
